Set in 12th-century England, with colourful descriptions of a tournament, outlaws, a witch trial, and divisions between Jews and Christians, Ivanhoe is credited for increased interest in chivalric romance and medievalism.

Main Characters:
- King Richard I
- Lady Rowena
- Rebecca
- Cedric the Saxon
- Prince John
- Locksley
- Isaac of York
- Wilfred of Ivanhoe 

Sir Walter Scott: (1771-1832)
- He was Scottish but many of his works are based in England.
Job: He was appointed sheriff depute to the county of Selkirk in 1799 and was also a partner in a printing firm owned by the Ballantyne brothers.

Best Works: 
- Ivanhoe
- Kenilworth
- Marmion
- Minstrelsy of the Scottish Border
- Old Mortality

- Rokeby
- Talisman
- The Chase and William and Helen

নতুনদের বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (১৫০ দিনে পুরো.option3: গ) Victory of Royal British family
নতুনদের বিসিএস প্রস্তুতি (১৫০ দিনে পুরো.exp:
Victorian Age: 
- Victorian period is named after Queen Victoria of England who reigned England from 1837 to 1901.
- But as the Romantic period ended in 1832, so it counts Victorian English Literary Period from 1832 to 1901.
- The 19th century is widely considered to be the Golden Age of English Literature, especially for British novels.
- It was in the Victorian era that the novel became the leading literary genre in English. - - English writing from this era reflects the major transformations in most aspects of English life, from scientific, economic, and technological advances to changes in class structures and the role of religion in society.
- Famous novelists from this period include Charles Dickens, William Thackeray, the three Brontë sisters, George Eliot, and Thomas Hardy.

Source: Britannica.com

The Return of the Native
- This is a novel written by Thomas Hardy.
-  It was first published in 1878.
- The novel is set on Egdon Heath, a fictional barren moor in Wessex in southwestern England.
- The native of the title is Clym Yeobright, who has returned to the area to become a schoolmaster after a successful but, in his opinion, shallow career as a jeweler in Paris.

Other great Novels:
- A Pair of Blue Eyes.
- Under The Greenwood Tree.
- The Mayor of Casterbridge etc.
-The Return of the Native.
-Tess of the D'Urbervilles.

Silas Marner:
In full, Silas Marner: The Weaver of Raveloe is the third novel by George Eliot. It was published in 1861. An outwardly simple tale of a linen weaver, the novel is notable for its strong realism and its sophisticated treatment of a variety of issues ranging from religion to industrialisation to community.

Major Characters:
- Silas Marner
- Squire Cass
- Dunstan Cass
- Eppie 
- Sarah
- Priscilla Lammete. Etc.

George Eliot(1819-80):
Her real name is Mary Ann Evans. She developed the psychological analysis of characters. 

Best Works: 
- Adam Bede (1859) 
- Silas Marner (1861) 
- Middlemarch (1871-72)
- Scenes of Clerical life (1858)
- The Mill on the Floss (1860)
- The Spanish Gypsy (tragi-comedy)
